FoodHub Data Analysis¶

Context¶

The number of restaurants in New York is increasing day by day. Lots of students and busy professionals rely on those restaurants due to their hectic lifestyles. Online food delivery service is a great option for them. It provides them with good food from their favorite restaurants. A food aggregator company FoodHub offers access to multiple restaurants through a single smartphone app.

The app allows the restaurants to receive a direct online order from a customer. The app assigns a delivery person from the company to pick up the order after it is confirmed by the restaurant. The delivery person then uses the map to reach the restaurant and waits for the food package. Once the food package is handed over to the delivery person, he/she confirms the pick-up in the app and travels to the customer's location to deliver the food. The delivery person confirms the drop-off in the app after delivering the food package to the customer. The customer can rate the order in the app. The food aggregator earns money by collecting a fixed margin of the delivery order from the restaurants.

Objective¶

The food aggregator company has stored the data of the different orders made by the registered customers in their online portal. They want to analyze the data to get a fair idea about the demand of different restaurants which will help them in enhancing their customer experience. Suppose you are hired as a Data Scientist in this company and the Data Science team has shared some of the key questions that need to be answered. Perform the data analysis to find answers to these questions that will help the company to improve the business.

Data Description¶

The data contains the different data related to a food order. The detailed data dictionary is given below.

Data Dictionary¶

  • order_id: Unique ID of the order
  • customer_id: ID of the customer who ordered the food
  • restaurant_name: Name of the restaurant
  • cuisine_type: Cuisine ordered by the customer
  • cost: Cost of the order
  • day_of_the_week: Indicates whether the order is placed on a weekday or weekend (The weekday is from Monday to Friday and the weekend is Saturday and Sunday)
  • rating: Rating given by the customer out of 5
  • food_preparation_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the restaurant to prepare the food. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the restaurant's order confirmation and the delivery person's pick-up confirmation.
  • delivery_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the delivery person to deliver the food package. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the delivery person's pick-up confirmation and drop-off information

Observations:¶

  1. Cost of the Order:
  • The distribution is right-skewed, indicating that most orders are low to moderately priced, with fewer orders having a very high cost.
  • The boxplot shows a median cost below $15, with a few outliers indicating some orders are significantly more expensive.
  1. Day of the Week:
  • Orders made on weekends are significantly more than that of weekdays, indicating which days are more popular for ordering.
  1. Cuisine Type:
  • American, Japanese, Italian, and Chinese cuisine are the top 4 most popular cuisine
  1. Food Preparation Time:
  • The distribution is fairly symmetrical, fairly evenly distributed across its range.
  1. Delivery Time:
  • Similar to food preparation time, this distribution is also fairly symmetrical.
  • Clear concentration around the mean and median (24-25 mins), indicating that most deliveries occur within a typical time frame (consistency)

Observations:¶

  1. Pairplot & heatmap - Numerical Variables:

No visible linear relationship between the numerical variables (cost_of_the_order, food_preparation_time, and delivery_time).

  1. Relationships between Categorical and Numerical Variables:
  • Day of the Week and Numerical Variables:

The day of the week doesn't seem to have a significant impact on the cost of the order AND food preparation time.HOWEVER, there seems to be an impact made on weekday delivery time. This is worth to dive deeper at since most orders came on weekends

  • Rating and Numerical Variables:

The distributions of the 3 numerical variables appear relatively uniform across different ratings, suggesting no significant variation of these numerical variables with respect to the ratings

  • Cuisine Type and Numerical Variables:
    vs Cost. There are notable differences in the median costs and the overall distribution of order costs among different cuisine types. This suggests that the cost is influenced by the type of cuisine, with some cuisines typically having higher or lower costs.
    vs Preparation time . Some cuisines show a broader range of preparation times than others, indicated by the size of the boxes and the spread of the whiskers and outliers.
    vs Delivery Time. There are variations to small extent, although the variations might not be as pronounced as with the cost and preparation time. Nonetheless, this indicates that certain cuisines might generally require more or less time for delivery
  1. Heatmap - Categorical variables (day of the week, rating, and cuisine_type)

Deeper dive on this is optional, but i can see that there were some insights that might be a point of consideration such as: all customer who eats spanish cuisine on weekdays historically didnt leave any rating, some days might consistently show higher or lower ratings across all or most cuisine types.

Question 14: The company charges the restaurant 25% on the orders having cost greater than 20 dollars and 15% on the orders having cost greater than 5 dollars. Find the net revenue generated by the company across all orders¶

In [40]:
# Write the code here
# i'll create a Function to calculate revenue based on cost_of_the_order 
def calculate_revenue(cost):
    if cost > 20:
        return cost * 0.25
    elif cost > 5:
        return cost * 0.15
    else:
        return 0

# Apply the function to the cost_of_the_order column and sum up the revenues (create new column)
df['revenue'] = df['cost_of_the_order'].apply(calculate_revenue)
total_revenue = df['revenue'].sum()

Question 15: The company wants to analyze the total time required to deliver the food. What percentage of orders take more than 60 minutes to get delivered from the time the order is placed? (The food has to be prepared and then delivered)¶

Conclusion and Recommendations¶

Question 17: What are your conclusions from the analysis? What recommendations would you like to share to help improve the business? (You can use cuisine type and feedback ratings to drive your business recommendations)¶

Conclusions:¶

  • Lack of Linear Relationship: Linear relationships among numerical variables (cost, preparation time, and delivery time) suggests that these variables influence each other in non-linear ways or are influenced more by external factors like cuisine type or operational efficiency.

  • Customer Rating Insights: Distribution of numerical variables across ratings implies that factors like cost, preparation, and delivery time might NOT directly influence how customers rate their experience. Other qualitative factors like food quality, customer service, and overall satisfaction may be worth to explore.

  • Revenue: The company generates substantial revenue from commissions (business model), particularly from higher-cost orders.

  • Delivery Times: Weekends deliveries are faster than on weekdays. Additionally, around 10.54% of total orders take longer than 60 mins, which could be room for improvement.

  • Order volume by days:Weekends see higher order volumes than weekdays, suggesting that users are more likely to order out on weekend

  • Cuisine Preferences: American, Japanese, Italian, and Chinese cuisines dominate in popularity, pointing towards a diverse customer base. with varied tastes. Preferences for American and Japanese cuisines are more during weekends.

  • Restaurant Popularity: Certain restaurants like Shake Shack, The Meatball Shop, and Blue Ribbon Sushi lead in order volumes, indicating strong brand preferences or better customer experiences at these places.

Recommendations:¶

  1. Focus on Higher Value Orders, Leverage Popular Restaurants
  • Given the revenue model, promoting high-value orders can significantly increase earnings. We can create incentives for customers to place larger orders, such as bundled deals or special discounts on combos.
  • Considering that 29.24% of orders are over $20, targeting these higher-value orders with specific promotions or loyalty benefits could boost revenue

Collaborate more closely with restaurants that consistently receive large orders to ensure their needs are med efficiently

  • Create exclusive deals or loyalty programs that encourage repeat business with the popular restaurants. Highlighting these restaurants in marketing materials could also attract new users.
  1. Optimize Weekdays Delivery
  • Investigate the reasons behind longer delivery times on weekdays (traffic conditions, delivery routes, staffing, etc.). If staffing model is the cause, we can implement dynamic staffing models
  1. Enhance Weekend Services
  • Since weekends are more popular for receiving orders, we need to ensure adequate staffing and possibly offering special weekend deals to capitalize on this trend
  • Also we can create partnerships with popular cuisine type providers on weekends to boost orders
  1. Cuisine Promotions
  • Certain cuisines are more popular than others, for example, we can feature American and Japanese cuisines more prominently on the platform during weekends
  1. Customer Incentives
  • Giving 20% discount vouchers to top 3 most frequentcustomer was not a bad idea (Q11). We can consider the expansion of such loyalty programs to include not just the frequency but also value of orders to encourage higher spending
  1. Maintain Consistency (Delivery Time) & Quality (Ratings)
  • Our current level of consistency (Total Time Required to Deliver the Food) based on the distribution plot is already quite consistent. However, still 200 orders take more than 60 minutes from placement to delivery (10.54%). We can implement a feedback system to monitor and improve the quality of both food and service time continuously could help in maintaining standards
  • Restaurants with consistently low ratings could be offered training or resources to improve their performance
  1. Technology Improvement
  • Invest in technology to better predict order preparation times and optimize delivery routes
  1. Infrastructure Improvement
  • Consider a tiered delivery fee structure where customers can choose faster delivery for a premium, potentially increasing customer satisfaction and revenue.
